key_insight: FFT-based acoustic emission features let an explainable AI pipeline distinguish good welds, porosity, and burn-through in TIG welding with near-perfect accuracy.
engineering_relevance: This enables real-time, non-destructive weld-condition monitoring for AA5083, supporting faster quality control and defect detection during production.
method: Acoustic emission was sampled at 10 kHz and converted to frequency-domain features using FFT; STFT was used to inspect time-varying behavior.
Decision Tree, SVM, ANN, and ensemble classifiers were trained on spectral features, with PCA used to reduce FFT dimensionality.
Five-fold cross-validation and grid-search tuning were used, and SHAP highlighted the most influential frequency bands.
evidence_signal: Using independently verified weld labels and a reserved test set, the best models achieved about 0.99 classification accuracy for three weld states.
watch_item: Performance was demonstrated on a specific alloy and setup, so broader robustness across other welding parameters, sensors, and shop-floor noise still needs validation.
paper_title: Acoustic Emission Metrology for Real-Time TIG Welding Monitoring: Spectral Characterization and Interpretability via Explainable AI
